content.title: About
content.content: Teriyaki sauce is a sweet‑savory Japanese condiment made from soy sauce, sake (or mirin), sugar, and ginger. It is used as a marinade, glaze, and seasoning for meat, fish, vegetables, and rice dishes.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Teriyaki means “bright sauce,” referring to its glossy, shiny finish after cooking.
The traditional recipe includes rice wine (sake) and mirin, but many commercial versions use corn syrup.
In Japan the sauce is often made at home, while in the US and Europe it became popular as a ready‑to‑use product.
Teriyaki can be light or dark; the dark version contains more soy sauce and caramelized sugar.
Vegetarian versions exist that omit fish ingredients and rely solely on plant‑based components.

items.title: Rich in plant protein
items.content: Soy sauce, the base of teriyaki, provides plant‑based protein that supports tissue repair.

items.title: Contains antioxidants
items.content: Ginger and garlic, common additions, are rich in antioxidants that help combat free radicals.

items.title: Supports digestion
items.content: Ginger stimulates gastric secretions, aiding digestion.

items.title: Lower sodium options available
items.content: Some modern recipes use low‑sodium soy sauce, reducing overall salt intake.

items.title: Adds flavor without excess fat
items.content: Teriyaki imparts a strong taste, allowing reduced oil use when cooking.

items.title: High sugar content
items.content: Teriyaki sauce often contains a significant amount of sugar, which can increase calories and affect blood glucose levels.

items.title: Sodium level
items.content: Traditional soy sauce is high in sodium; people with hypertension should choose reduced‑salt versions.

items.title: Soy allergy
items.content: Individuals allergic to soy should avoid teriyaki sauce or use alternatives based on coconut aminos.

items.title: Monosodium glutamate (MSG)
items.content: Some commercial sauces add MSG, which may cause sensitivity in certain individuals.

content.title: How to Use
content.content: Teriyaki sauce works well for marinating chicken, beef, pork, and tofu, as a glaze for grilling, in stir‑fries, as a dipping sauce for sushi rolls, and as a dip for vegetables. It can be thinned with water or broth for a lighter consistency.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store teriyaki sauce in a tightly sealed bottle in the refrigerator after opening. It typically remains good for 6–12 months. Discard if the smell, color, or texture changes or if sediment appears.
